Definition: from the base of G4226 and G3634; individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one:--what (manner of), which.
BiblicalUsage: Poios means what sort, of what kind — the question word for character, not identity. The chief priests ask Jesus, By what authority doest thou these things, in Matthew 21:23, and the lawyer asks, What commandment is first, in Mark 12:28. The prophets searched what manner of time the Spirit of Christ signified, says 1 Peter 1:11.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what sort is the question that matters most — not who, but what kind.
